description:
**Divergence**: the workspace expresses 'is this property per-user-scoped?' in two incompatible places across two sibling crates.

- TasksBackend::is_per_user_property (crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:209):
    /// Default returns true for {keywords, color, freeBusyStatus, useDefaultAlerts, alerts}.
    fn is_per_user_property(&self, prop: &str) -> bool { ... hardcoded set ... }
  Seam location: TRAIT METHOD with default impl. Backends CAN override.
- CalendarsBackend (crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:295-297 rustdoc):
    Calendars' equivalent is a free function jmap_calendars_types::is_per_user_calendar_event_property
    referenced from rustdoc; called by the handler before reaching the trait. Seam location: TYPES CRATE FREE FN.
    Backends CANNOT override.

**Caller-observable effect**: a third-party backend author who needs to alter the per-user property set:
- In tasks-server: overrides `is_per_user_property` on their backend impl. Works.
- In calendars-server: cannot. The predicate lives in jmap-calendars-types and is hardcoded into the calendars-server handler call site.

**Reverse caller-observable effect** for a kit-author wanting to evolve the predicate:
- In tasks-server: bumping the default predicate set is a semver-breaking change to TasksBackend (downstream backends that overrode the default with a fixed string set might silently misalign).
- In calendars-server: bumping the predicate set in jmap-calendars-types is a semver-breaking change to the types crate.

**Neither sibling is the canonical template here** — mail-server and chat-server have no per-user property concept, so there's no third sibling to disambiguate. This is a workspace-architecture decision that needs to land before either contacts-server or filenode-server grow per-user-property semantics and have to pick a side.

**Two recommended resolutions**:
(a) Predicate-on-backend-trait (tasks shape): move calendars's `is_per_user_calendar_event_property` from jmap-calendars-types to a default method on CalendarsBackend with the same signature as TasksBackend::is_per_user_property. Backends become the canonical authority. The types-crate free function becomes a backwards-compat shim that the calendars-server handler stops calling.
(b) Predicate-in-types-crate (calendars shape): move tasks's `is_per_user_property` from TasksBackend to a free function `jmap_tasks_types::is_per_user_task_property`. Handlers call the free function directly. Backends lose the override seam.

Position (a) gives backends more control (consistent with workspace 'backends are canonical for permission enforcement' pattern); position (b) gives kit authors more control over evolution. Pick one and propagate.
title: tasks-server / calendars-server: per-user property predicate lives on the backend trait vs in the types crate — two seams, neither canonical
